title: Phenotypic differences between interfertile Chlamydomonas species- timelapse microscopy data, part 2
author: Garcia III, Galo
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Collect cells from agar plates
steps.instruction: Harvest Chlamydomonas cells from agar plates using a sterile loop or pipette.

steps.title: Suspend cells in water
steps.instruction: Resuspend the harvested cells in sterile distilled water to create a cell suspension.

steps.title: Incubate overnight for gamete formation
steps.instruction: Allow the suspension to sit overnight at room temperature to promote gamete formation; during this period non‑motile cells settle, enriching motile cells in the supernatant.

steps.title: Harvest motile cell supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully collect the supernatant containing the enriched motile cells without disturbing the settled non‑motile cells.

steps.title: Load cells into agar microchambers
steps.instruction: Introduce the motile cell suspension into agar microchambers that are 100 µm in diameter and 40 µm deep.

steps.title: Configure microscope for DIC imaging
steps.instruction: Set up a Nikon Ti2‑E microscope equipped with a Photometrics Kinetix digital sCMOS camera; install a Plan Apo 10× 0.45 Air objective; place an IR long‑pass red light filter (610 nm, Thorlabs) in the light path to maintain swimming behavior; select differential interference contrast (DIC) mode.

steps.title: Acquire timelapse video
steps.instruction: Record videos with a 5.1 ms exposure, acquiring frames every 50 ms for a total of three minutes (≈3601 frames, 20 fps, pixel size 0.6398 µm/pixel).

steps.title: Repeat experiment for consistency
steps.instruction: Perform the entire procedure four independent times to ensure reproducibility.
